reviews.comment: Really nice and caring guy, but he didn't seem to understand that 229 is for students just starting accounting. His lectures were hard to follow, and he didn't explain concepts well when asked. After barely passing the first test, I switched to Knoop's lectures and learned much more. Great person, just not the best fit for beginners.

Professor Garza utilizes AI to grade all written portions, but he also openly allows students to use AI to further their education. One thing I wished his summer section did was cover more accounting background, so we could better apply audit knowledge covered in class. Exams are rough, as they are CPA-style. Great guy & super accessible if needed

Professor Garza is great. He is extremely willing to sit down and explain all the ins and outs that you may be confused about. The course itself is difficult; however, if you have any questions, reaching out is necessary. Tests are difficult if you don't know the content well. IMO difficulty is on par with ACCT 327 because content is unfamiliar.

Professor Garza is probably one of the nicest people I've ever met. That being said this class was extraordinarily hard for me to follow in. I have always been a solid A student with the hard work I put in and this class was definitely an exception. He however is so willing to sit down in his office hours and one on one explain things to you.

Absolutely my favorite professor ever he truly cares so much about his students and was very motivating and inspirational, he made me fall in love with accounting. If you're reading this know this is from Buck

Professor Garza's lectures were very difficult to follow. He teaches in a very confusing way often going into hypotheticals when talking about accounting and not explaining problems until he has completed them, making it hard to follow. I learned more from Knoop's videos than I did his lectures.

Professor Garza is such a nice person, and his class was very easy to work through, especially after working all of those hours post-internship. There are lots of assignments during the course, but they are all very straightforward, and Garza was there to help every step of the way. Professor Head I've heard is great as well, so you can't go wrong.
The best professor I have ever had, he made me fall in love with accounting and is very responsive to emails and very caring about his students. If you're seeing this, this is from Buck

Always felt very well prepared for tests going off the in class lectures and practice problems he posted. Very helpful in class, and clearly passionate about the subject. ACCT 229 can be difficult however he certainly prepared the class well for all exams.
Definitely knows what he's talking about but not necessarily the best way to teach it. He's very nice but I'm not sure his teaching style is the easiest to follow along with. Hard class overall
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely vague and ambiguous and do not prepare you for the exam. Test questions have confusing wording because they all come from CPA test prep books.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I am leaving this class having no better an idea of what it is then when I got here. His lectures are just so ambiguous and have no clear path or information. They are extremely broad and open to interpretation He is so freaking nice but unfortunately not the best professor. Honestly very easy B though

Overall the class was doable, if you don't mind teaching yourself/ reading the book outside of class. Lectures are repetitive and we got super behind schedule. The exams are like the CPA exam and involve LOTS of critical thinking. He released test grades during the BAMA game... and thought it was so funny! Auditors sell what?...TRUST!

His audit class is very difficult and requires weekly homework and assignments. He uses questions from the CPA on his exams which are difficult. However, he's very nice and a good grade is definitely doable if you work for it.
